question.worked_solution:
Using the fact that $4=\frac{4}{1},$ we can write the expression as

$$
\frac{4}{1}+\frac{4}{n}.
$$

 

In order to add the two fractions, we need them to have a common denominator. So, we put both fractions over a common denominator of $n$ by multiplying the top and bottom of the first fraction by $n:$

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{4}{1}+\frac{4}{n} & = \\ \frac{n}{n}\cdot \frac{4}{1}+\frac{4}{n} & = \\ \frac{4n}{n}+\frac{4}{n}\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we add the fractions and simplify the result:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{4n}{n}+\frac{4}{n} & = \\ \frac{4n+4}{n} & = \\ \frac{4(n+1)}{n}\end{aligned}
$$
